title: Garlands, tika and treats: Nepal Embassy celebrates Kukur Tihar in Delhi - The Tribune
description: Garlands, tika and treats: Nepal Embassy celebrates Kukur Tihar in Delhi  The Tribune
publisher.title: The Tribune
full_article:
For once, the spotlight was not on the diplomats, but on their four-legged companions.

Adorned with bright marigold garlands, their foreheads marked with red tika and treated to special delicacies, dogs were the stars of the day as the Embassy of Nepal in New Delhi celebrated Kukur Tihar on Sunday.

The celebration brought together members of the Nepali community, diplomats and embassy staff, who gathered to honour the animals in keeping with a cherished tradition of their homeland.

For Nepalis, Kukur Tihar is an expression of gratitude towards animals whose loyalty, companionship and protective instincts have earned them a special place in human lives.

Observed as part of the five-day Tihar festival, also known as Yamapanchak or Deepawali, Kukur Tihar falls on the second day of the celebrations. This year, it was observed on November 8, coinciding with Laxmi Puja in the evening.

Across Nepal, the day sees dogs, whether pampered household pets or street companions, receiving special attention. They are adorned with marigold garlands, have vermilion tika applied to their foreheads and are offered food ranging from rice, meat and eggs to sweets.

The tradition has deep roots in Hindu mythology. Dogs are associated with Yama, the god of death, and are believed to serve as his messengers and guardians. They are also regarded as sentinels who guard the gates of the underworld.

title: Nepal wins first-ever gold medal at Junior International Astronomy Olympiad - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Nepal wins first-ever gold medal at Junior International Astronomy Olympiad  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Kathmandu, November 8

Nepal has won its first-ever gold medal at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics – Junior (IOAA-jr), with a student securing the top award at the competition held in Thailand.

At the fifth edition of the competition, held in Ubon Ratchathani from November 1 to 8, Nepal won one gold medal, one bronze medal and one honourable mention.

Shahwaz Alam won the gold medal, marking the first time a Nepali student has won gold in the history of the International Science Olympiads, according to the Nepal Astronomical Society (NASO).

Sahaj KC secured a bronze medal, while Evan Dubey received an honourable mention. Abhi Udaya Dhungana and Akhilesh Pokharel also represented Nepal in the competition.

The students were selected through the National Astronomy Olympiad (NAO) 2026, organised by NASO, followed by a closed-camp training programme. The team also attended an intensive pre-departure training camp before travelling to Thailand.

The Nepali team was led by team leaders Manisha Dwa and Oshan Sharma Kattel.

Nepal had previously won bronze medals in international astronomy competitions, including the International Astronomy Olympiad (IAO) and the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA). The gold medal at the junior edition marks a new milestone for the country’s participation in international science competitions.

NASO congratulated the students, team leaders, parents and supporters for their contribution to the achievement.

title: Nepal Police Utilize Dogs for Crime Investigation, Search and Rescue - Ratopati
description: Nepal Police Utilize Dogs for Crime Investigation, Search and Rescue  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal Police have been using dogs for crime investigation, peace security, and disaster management. Police officials say that the use of dogs is proving effective in successful crime investigation and human search and rescue.

Starting with 4 dogs in 2026 BS, the Police Canine Office currently has 107 trained dogs in 13 locations across the country. In the last year, police dogs have achieved significant success in identifying perpetrators of serious crimes like murder and in searching for bodies and human remains in disasters like floods and landslides.

Police have been deploying tracker dogs in complex murder and crime investigations, said the Chief of the Police Canine Office (SP) Dr. Ramchandra Satyal. Police used dogs in the investigation of the murder of 19-year-old Bhola Sahani of Baragadhi Mai Bagarampur, who went missing on Kartik 10, 2082 BS. When the dog sniffed the black hoodie found at the scene, it tracked for about 2 kilometers to Subodh Ram's house. During the investigation, he confessed to the murder.

Dogs were successful in the case where 55-year-old Bhishma Poudel was found dead inside the building of the Raghuganga Hydropower Project in Magdi's Raghuganga-3, found dead in a pond on Magh 15, 2082 BS. A German Shepherd named 'Tyson' sniffed a piece of iron found at the scene and signaled the security guard of the same building. On the same day, in the case of the murder of two men in Shuklagandaki-5 Kasarighat, Tanahun, and a woman with her throat slit on the bank of the Seti River about 1.5 kilometers away, 'Tyson' tracked for 4 kilometers to the Prithvi Highway and the location where the woman's body was found, by sniffing a plastic glass and bowl found at the scene.

On Bhadra 31, 2083 BS, the tracker team deployed for the investigation of the murder of about 4-year-old Garima Chaudhary of Jitpur Simara-1 signaled magic co-driver Suman Thapa and driver Progress Chaudhary by sniffing the victim's clothes. In the case where the body of 40-year-old Juvida Khatun Dhobi of Kothimai-5 was found in a field on Kartik 12, 2083 BS, dogs also conducted a successful investigation. Investigation officers tracked for about 3.5 kilometers using dogs by sniffing a sickle found near the body.

On Bhadra 10, 2083 BS, dogs deployed in Rasuwa and Nuwakot played a significant role in searching for citizens missing in the flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa. The Chief of the Police Canine Office (SP) Dr. Satyal said that dogs also gave excellent results in the search and rescue after the Bhote Koshi flood. Two dogs deployed from the Police Canine Office found two bodies and one body part in the Timure area on Bhadra 17.

Two dogs deployed in Nuwakot found bodies, skeletons, and body parts from various locations in Mailung Hydropower, Battar, Betrawati, Tupche Akkare, Devighat, Bidur-3, and Trishuli Bazaar from Bhadra 17 to 28.

A dog deployed from the Bagmati Province Police Canine Branch Hetauda to collect bodies found two bodies in the Daumli Golaghat area on Bhadra 18. The Police Canine Office stated that two dogs deployed from the Gandaki Province for body collection after the Bhote Koshi flood found human body parts in Siltingtar, Shahid Lakhan-3, Gorkha on Bhadra 21.

The Labrador Retriever breed male dog 'Leo', specialized in human search and rescue after the Bhote Koshi flood, has been declared the best police dog of the year. DIG Om Rana of the Police Headquarters presented the award to Leo at a program organized at the Police Canine Office in Maharajgunj on Sunday. Born on Ashad 9, 2078 BS, Leo has been serving at the Nepal Police Canine Office Maharajgunj for the past 4 years. During the rescue operation after the Bhote Koshi flood, Leo played an important role in finding 2 bodies, 1 skeleton, and small body parts in Nuwakot.

Police have been using dogs for drug detection and identification, explosive substance detection and identification, and human search and rescue. Police have 6 breeds of dogs for disaster management, rescue, and investigation. Labrador, German Shepherd, Belgian Shepherd, Golden Retriever, Cocker Spaniel, and Beagle breeds of dogs assist the police in investigation. Dogs have an extremely high sense of smell. Dogs used in search and rescue and investigation have 250 million olfactory cells. Normal dogs do not have that many olfactory cells.

Development and Current Structure

In 2026 BS, 5 police personnel who went to Malaysia for training started using dogs in police investigation with 4 dogs – 2 received with the assistance of the Malaysian government and 2 purchased in Nepal. In 2032 BS, the 'Dog Branch' was established with a strength of 10 people under the command of a Police Sub-Inspector. In 2047 BS, it was named 'Central Police Dog Training School', in 2075 BS 'Canine Division', and in 2078 BS 'Nepal Police Canine Office'.

Currently, the Canine Office operates with a sanctioned strength of 164 police personnel in 16 locations across the country. With 107 police dogs of 6 breeds, dog branches are currently operated in 13 locations.

Apart from Nepal Police Canine Office Maharajgunj, trained police dogs are stationed at Tribhuvan International Airport, Dharan, Biratnagar Airport, Lalgarh, Janakpur Airport, Birgunj, Hetauda, Pokhara, Bhairahawa's Gautam Buddha International Airport, Kohalpur, and Dhangadhi.

title: Sabina Kafle Advocates for Internationalizing Kukur Tihar Festival - Ratopati
description: Sabina Kafle Advocates for Internationalizing Kukur Tihar Festival  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Prime Minister Balen Shah's wife Sabina Kafle has stressed the need to internationalize festivals like Kukur Tihar to introduce the human relationship with Nepali indigenous culture, tradition, and nature to the world.

On the occasion of Kukur Tihar, 2083, the First Lady, Kafle, expressed the view at a goodwill exchange program organized here that our festivals and cultures, which have a unique tradition of respecting and conserving animals and nature, should be internationalized and promoted.

She stated that Kukur Tihar should be presented to the world not just as a religious and cultural festival, but as an opportunity to convey the message of love, loyalty, compassion, and coexistence towards animals. In the global context where love and attraction towards dogs are increasing worldwide, she said that Nepal can establish the unique cultural tradition of worshipping dogs as an international identity.

“Internationalizing Kukur Tihar is one of our main objectives. We want to convey the message of our unique tradition of worshipping and respecting dogs to the world from Nepal,” Kafle said.

She emphasized the need to conduct various activities for animal welfare throughout the year, rather than limiting Kukur Tihar to a one-day celebration. She pointed out the need for responsibility and uniformity in the proper management, vaccination, health treatment, and behavior towards dogs.

Kafle mentioned that Nepali festivals have many unique practices that reflect respect for nature and animals, and expressed the view that along with Kukur Tihar, Kag Puja, Gai Puja, Nag Puja, the Newar community's Mha Puja, and Chhath festival should also be promoted internationally. The tradition of performing frog marriages during dry spells is also an example of the relationship between nature and humans, she said.

Stating that in the 'digital' age, relationships between people and the proximity between humans and nature are weakening, she said that Nepali indigenous festivals can convey the message of re-establishing the relationship with nature.

Through the program, hashtags such as ‘From Nepal With Paws’, ‘Days of the Dogs’, ‘Visit Nepal Dog Stay’, ‘Love Your Dogs Every Day’, and ‘Kukur Tihar Nepal’ were also released to promote Kukur Tihar globally, she informed.

She urged policy-making officials, parliamentarians, local government representatives, artists, content producers, international media, and ambassadors from various countries to help promote this unique tradition of Nepal. “Our festivals have many unique aspects that connect the relationship between nature and humans. A common effort from everyone is necessary to take those aspects worldwide,” she said.

On the occasion, Minister of Agriculture, Forest, and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, said that Kukur Tihar should not be limited to a one-day religious tradition of worship but should be an expression of compassion, love, and responsibility towards animals throughout the year. She stated that animal welfare and human health are complementary subjects and that cooperation from the government, local levels, and all stakeholders is necessary for rabies control, vaccination, sterilization, and responsible animal husbandry under the ‘One Health Concept’.

Minister Chaudhary said that cooperation can be sought with Nepali embassies, Nepali communities abroad, tourism promotion bodies, and international animal welfare organizations to promote Kukur Tihar internationally. She said this would also contribute to the promotion of Nepal's unique culture and cultural tourism.

Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Khadakraj Poudel, discussed the relationship between dogs and humans and stated that Kukur Tihar holds special significance.

“The relationship between dogs and humans has existed from the beginning, dogs have special importance in our religions and cultures, and the importance of dogs is also mentioned in our scriptures,” he said.

On the occasion, Sabina Kafle worshipped a dog named Bindu. Artists Basundhara Bhusal, Bhuvan Thapa, and Mithila Sharma also specially honored ‘Samba’, a trained dog from the Armed Police's Canine Unit. On the occasion of Kukur Tihar, participants also worshipped their dogs.

description: QUICK TAKE | Why Nepal Puts Garlands on Dogs for Kukur Tihar. Seven Things to Know  Open Magazine
publisher.title: Open Magazine
full_article:
1. What is Kukur Tihar?

It is the second day of Tihar, Nepal’s five-day festival of lights. Kukur means dog in Nepali. The day follows Kaag Tihar, when people honour crows, and gives dogs their own place in the festival’s sequence of rituals.

2. What do people do for the dogs?

They place flower garlands around their necks, put a vermilion tika on their foreheads and offer them food. The ritual extends to street dogs as well as household pets. A dog can receive a garland and a meal from people it has never met.

3. What do dogs have to do with Yama?

In the tradition behind Tihar, dogs are regarded as agents of Yama, the Hindu god of death. The crow honoured on the first day is regarded as his messenger. The Nepal Tourism Board describes both rituals as part of a festival that also honours Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth.

4. Where does the Mahabharata come in?

A dog accompanies Yudhishthira on his final journey. When offered passage to heaven, he refuses to go without his companion. The dog then reveals himself as Dharma, who has been testing Yudhishthira’s conduct. The episode gives the festival another way to think about loyalty, including what people owe the animals that stay with them.

title: Nepal U-19 Cricket Team Suffers Second Consecutive Loss in ACC U-19 Asia Cup - Ratopati
description: Nepal U-19 Cricket Team Suffers Second Consecutive Loss in ACC U-19 Asia Cup  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal has suffered its second consecutive defeat in the ACC U-19 Asia Cup currently underway in Oman. Nepal was defeated by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in a Group 'A' match on Sunday.

Earlier, Nepal was defeated by India by 10 wickets in the first match of the tournament. With consecutive losses in two matches, Nepal's chances of reaching the semi-finals have weakened. Batting first against the UAE, Nepal was all out for 153 runs in 41 overs. The team could not set a competitive total as Nepali batsmen failed to form significant partnerships.

Sohail Kunwar scored a maximum of 33 runs for Nepal. He hit 3 fours off 71 balls. Sachin Bhatta scored 32 runs off 55 balls. Darsh Sonar and Niraj Kumar Yadav scored 16 runs each, while Ashish Luhar scored 11 runs.

UAE's Nasim Khan took 5 wickets in dismantling Nepal's batting. Ayan Misbah took 3 wickets and Nurullah Ayubi took 2 wickets. Nepal's batting also appeared weak in the first match against India. In that match, Nepal was all out for 128 runs in 42.3 overs.

India completed the target in just 19.1 overs without losing any wickets. India's Aryaveer Sehrawat remained unbeaten on 70 runs. Nepal's Darsh Sonar had scored 43 runs. India's Ishan Sood took 3 wickets.

With Nepal's second consecutive loss in the tournament, its chances of advancing from the group stage have become very difficult. Group 'A' consists of Nepal, India, Pakistan, and the UAE. The top two teams from this group will qualify for the semi-finals.

Nepal will play its final group stage match against Pakistan on Tuesday. To keep its chances of reaching the semi-finals alive, Nepal must win against Pakistan. However, the results of other teams and the net run rate equation will also be important for that.

Eight teams are participating in the ACC U-19 Asia Cup. Group 'A' includes Nepal, India, Pakistan, and the UAE, while Group 'B' includes Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia. After the group stage matches, the top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals. The final of the tournament will be held on November 14.

title: Nepal clinch U-19 women’s cricket title unbeaten in China - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal clinch U-19 women’s cricket title unbeaten in China  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal’s U-19 women’s cricket team have won the Belt and Road Series in China, finishing the tournament unbeaten after their final match against Hong Kong was abandoned due to rain on Sunday.

Nepal won four of their six matches in the four-team tournament, while the other two were abandoned due to rain.

Nepal made a winning start by defeating Thailand by seven wickets in their opening match. Their second match against hosts China was affected by rain and ended without a result. Nepal then registered a comprehensive 92-run victory over Hong Kong before beating Thailand by 52 runs in their fourth match.

Nepal strengthened their bid for the title with an 84-run victory over hosts China in their fifth match before taking on Hong Kong in the final fixture.

Batting first, Nepal had scored 88 runs for the loss of two wickets in 11 overs when rain interrupted play. The match could not resume due to adverse weather conditions, allowing Nepal to finish the series unbeaten and secure the title.
